title: feat(client): coalesce adjacent ranges in GcsBidiReadChannel.readVectored()
hypothesis: GcsBidiReadChannel.readVectored() issues one BlobReadSession.readAs() per range while GcsReadChannel (HTTP) coalesces adjacent ranges with VectoredIoUtil.mergeGcsObjectRanges() per GcsVectoredReadOptions. Applying the same coalescing to the bidi path reduces per-range server round trips for Parquet column-chunk reads and gives transport parity.
learning: Bidi vectored coalescing reused VectoredIoUtil wholesale (2 files/216 lines); ReadAsFutureByteString has value equals so Mockito can verify exact RangeSpec without captors; VectoredIoUtil.canMerge is strict (gap < maxMergeGap). Draft PR #404.

title: feat(core): serve vectored tail ranges from the cached footer in GcsFooterOptimizer
hypothesis: GcsFooterOptimizer does not override FormatOptimizer.readVectored(), so Parquet PageIndex/BloomFilter/footer tail ranges inside the already-cached footer window are re-fetched from GCS. Serving them from the cached footer buffer removes those tail RPCs with no extra network I/O.
learning: FormatOptimizer.readVectored hook existed but GcsFooterOptimizer never overrode it; serving window ranges from the cached footer needs only ~100 LOC and a no-load cache probe (loader that throws). Draft PR #405.

title: fix(client): short-circuit zero-length vectored ranges and validate offsets up front
hypothesis: A zero-length GcsObjectRange passed to GcsBidiReadChannel.readVectored() becomes RangeSpec.of(offset, 0), which java-storage interprets as 'read to EOF', so the caller receives the whole object tail instead of an empty buffer; GcsReadChannel opens an unnecessary ranged RPC for the same input, and a negative offset/length in the bidi path throws mid-loop leaving sibling futures hanging. Validating ranges up front and short-circuiting zero-length ranges with an empty buffer aligns both transports with the Hadoop/Iceberg tail-range edge cases.
learning: java-storage RangeSpec.of(offset, 0) means read-to-EOF: zero-length vectored ranges on the bidi path returned the whole object tail. Fixed with a shared VectoredIoUtil pre-validation helper (6 files/271 lines). Draft PR #406.

title: test(core): add hermetic JMH micro-benchmarks for GoogleCloudStorageInputStream
hypothesis: Benchmarks that drive GoogleCloudStorageInputStream through an in-memory Storage (no network) measure library CPU/allocation overhead with low variance, giving the perf gate a trustworthy, credential-free signal.
learning: Hermetic JMH (InMemoryStorage Proxy + HermeticGcsFileSystem via createStorage seam) runs with no bucket; 398 lines in 3 files. positionedReads allocates ~275KB per stream open -> future perf lead. Primary checkout has a pre-push patent guard; loop now runs from gcs-analytics-core-sil clone.

title: fix(client): short-circuit zero-length vectored ranges and validate offsets up front
hypothesis: Revision of PR #406 after review: pre-size the ImmutableList builder in VectoredIoUtil.completeDegenerateRanges with the input size so the common all-valid path does not pay capacity-4 geometric regrowth. Behaviour unchanged.
learning: Rev 2 of PR #406 after Argon/Fable review: builderWithExpectedSize only; gates PASS unchanged. Review consensus: no PR adds RPCs; must-fix items were all in #405 (throwing-loader probe on default-on path, over-copy, unguarded allocator).

title: feat(core): serve vectored tail ranges from the cached footer in GcsFooterOptimizer
hypothesis: Revision of PR #405 after review: probe the shared footer cache with a new Optional-returning AnalyticsCacheManager.getFooterIfPresent() instead of a throwing loader (no exceptions, no Caffeine compute lock, works with the default NoOp footer cache), cap the copy at the requested length for oversized allocator buffers, settle every range future even if the allocator throws, count hits only on successful completion, and keep the common data-page path allocation-free.
learning: Rev 2 of PR #405: never probe a cache with a throwing loader (default footer cache is NoOp -> exception per call; Caffeine compute lock otherwise) - use AnalyticsCache.get(K)/getFooterIfPresent. Optimizers must settle every future themselves: SmartReadChannel.readVectored has no try/catch, so an optimizer exception strands all later futures. Cap copies at range length; rewind to start position, do not flip().

title: test(test-lib): add InMemoryStorage fake and HermeticGcsFileSystem factory
hypothesis: Hosting the zero-copy InMemoryStorage fake and a HermeticGcsFileSystem factory in test-lib (which already splits the client package) gives unit tests and benchmarks one credential-free Storage substrate whose ReadChannel contract is proven against the SDK's real channel via LocalStorageHelper.
learning: PR A of hermetic-module stack: fakes moved to test-lib (393 lines). Critic caught 3 majors on first pass: Proxy Object-methods, non-daemon pool threads, getGcsItemInfo must throw FileNotFoundException like production. Contract test split to PR A' to respect the 400-line gate.

title: feat(client): coalesce adjacent ranges in GcsBidiReadChannel.readVectored()
hypothesis: Revision of PR #404 after review, stacked on the zero-length range fix: GcsBidiReadChannel.readVectored() coalesces nearby ranges with the same VectoredIoUtil rules and GcsVectoredReadOptions as the HTTP path, feeding the already-validated pending ranges straight into the merge (no redundant copy), allocating min(bytesRead, combinedLength) and rejecting over-long responses with a descriptive IOException instead of a BufferOverflowException.
learning: Rev 2 of PR #404 stacked on #406: hygiene counts the whole stack vs base, so a stacked PR must budget for the lower PR's lines (272 + 124). Critic rejected one round for dropping a test to fit the cap - trim redundant verifies, never tests. java-storage: each readAs sends its own BidiReadObjectRequest + lock-held scan of outstanding reads, which justifies coalescing on bidi.

title: test(test-lib): add InMemoryStorage ReadChannel contract test against the SDK channel
hypothesis: Running one ReadChannel contract suite against both InMemoryStorage and the SDK's real channel (via LocalStorageHelper) proves the fake preserves seek/absolute-limit/EOF/close semantics, so benchmark and unit-test results over the fake transfer to production strategies.
learning: PR A' (stacked on A): ReadChannel contract suite vs SDK channel via LocalStorageHelper; FakeStorageRpc zero-pads past limit so that one case is excluded for the oracle. First stacked PR: --stack-on + merge-base baseline fallback both worked.

title: build(benchmarks): add benchmarks module with hermetic input-stream JMH suite
hypothesis: A never-published, always-in-reactor benchmarks module with JMH in src/main and a JUnit smoke test in src/test keeps hermetic benchmarks compiled under Error Prone/Spotless on JDK 11/17/21 and executed on every PR, so they cannot bit-rot and the perf gate can run them without credentials.
learning: PR B: benchmarks module (400/400 lines). combine.children=append keeps Error Prone active; jacoco.skip + codecov ignore verified; counters exposed real I/O-shape leads (109 opens for 64x4KiB positioned reads). Critic nit: source.skip redundant. release-please bump of new child pom unverified -> check on first release PR.

title: refactor(benchmarks): move GCS-backed JMH benchmarks and the jmh profile out of core
hypothesis: Relocating the five GCS-backed JMH benchmarks and the jmh profile from core/root into benchmarks/src/jmh-e2e (opt-in -Pjmh) gives one home for all benchmark tiers, removes the root exec-maven-plugin that fires on every reactor module, and keeps the default build free of Hadoop/Parquet and credentials.
learning: PR C (stacked on B): moved 9 GCS-backed JMH files via pure git mv (R100, 0 changed lines) into benchmarks/src/jmh-e2e and relocated the jmh profile from root+core into benchmarks/pom.xml (300/400 lines). Profile maven-compiler-plugin <excludes> merges cleanly with module-level combine.children=append annotationProcessorPaths.

title: test(benchmarks): add read-strategy, optimizer and coalescing hermetic benchmarks
hypothesis: Hermetic benchmarks for read strategies, per-open cost, footer prefetch, small-object cache, vectored coalescing and telemetry/cache overhead, paired with zero-noise JUnit reader-open invariants, cover the remaining hot paths so perf regressions in any tier are caught without credentials.
learning: PR D (stacked on C): added ReadStrategyBenchmark, FooterPrefetchBenchmark, SmallObjectCacheBenchmark, VectoredRangeCoalescingBenchmark, and ReaderOpenInvariantsTest (392/400 lines). Critic caught coldRead creating a fresh HermeticGcsFileSystem (and ThreadPoolExecutor) per invocation; fixed via cacheManager.invalidateSmallObject(itemId). Exposed perf lead: warm SmallObjectCache reads still do 1 eager 0-byte reader open in GcsReadChannel.<init>.

title: test(benchmarks): add channel-open and telemetry/cache overhead hermetic benchmarks
hypothesis: Adding GcsReadChannelOpenBenchmark (open with GcsFileInfo vs GcsItemId) and TelemetryOverheadBenchmark (Telemetry NoOp vs custom OperationListeners and Caffeine vs NoOp cache) completes hermetic benchmark coverage across client and common hot paths.
learning: PR D' (stacked on D): added GcsReadChannelOpenBenchmark and TelemetryOverheadBenchmark (226/400 lines). Critic caught empty OperationListener callbacks allowing C2 scalar replacement of MetricKey/singletonMap (consuming into volatile sink moved recordMetric from 3.0 to 11.7 ns/op). Exposed 7.8x open overhead on unknown-size GcsReadChannel from uncached reflective probe exceptions.

title: test(benchmarks): record per-op IoCounters delta and wire remaining benchmarks
hypothesis: IoCounters uses @AuxCounters(Type.EVENTS) with +=, so JMH emits total events per 1s iteration (opens_per_op * allOps) which varies with CPU throughput. Recording the per-invocation delta (= instead of +=) and wiring IoCounters into sequentialRead and readTailWithFooterPrefetch gives exact per-operation I/O counts (#/op) with zero variance across all 28 I/O benchmark cases.
learning: IoCounters @AuxCounters(Type.EVENTS) resets once per 1s iteration, so += scaled with CPU throughput; = records the exact per-op delta (#/op) with sd=0 across all 28 I/O benchmark cases. Promoted to PR #414.

title: perf(client): cache reflective metadata accessors per channel class
hypothesis: GcsReadChannelMetadataExtractor.extract() walks the ReadChannel class hierarchy calling getDeclaredMethod/getDeclaredField with setAccessible(true) across 9 candidate names and calls target.getClass().getMethods() (cloning the entire Method[] array and allocating Streams) up to 3 times per open (including extracting size twice via hasValidMetadata and extract); caching resolved Class<?> accessors via ClassValue eliminates ~6.3 KiB/op of reflection allocations and cuts itemId channel open latency by ~50%.
learning: ClassValue caching of ChannelAccessors/PropertyAccessors in GcsReadChannelMetadataExtractor cut openAndReadOneByte_withItemId latency by 70.1% (2.96->0.89 us/op) and alloc by 73.3% (9432->2516 B/op), improving 23/45 hermetic benchmarks with 0 regressions. Critic caught unhandled InaccessibleObjectException on setAccessible(true) in PropertyAccessors; fixed and tested via jrt:/ BasicFileAttributes.

title: perf(client): avoid per-channel 128 KiB skipBuffer allocation on seek
hypothesis: Replacing the per-instance 128 KiB skipBuffer field in AbstractReadStrategy with a per-thread ThreadLocal<SoftReference<ByteBuffer>> eliminates a 131,072 B heap allocation and array-zeroing cost per strategy instance on in-place forward seeks within inplaceSeekLimit, cutting ReadStrategyBenchmark.seekAndRead allocation by ~93% (~140.5 KiB/op -> ~9.4 KiB/op) and latency by ~65-70% across all 6 forward-gap cases while preserving thread isolation and GC reclaimability.
learning: Replaced per-instance 128 KiB skipBuffer in AbstractReadStrategy with ThreadLocal<SoftReference<ByteBuffer>>, cutting ReadStrategyBenchmark.seekAndRead allocation by -93.3% (140.5 KiB/op -> 9.4 KiB/op) and latency by -63.2% to -73.3% across all 6 forward-gap cases, plus HermeticInputStreamBenchmark.positionedReads(1 MiB) allocation by -51.9% and latency by -36.3%. Raised upstream PR #422.

title: perf(client): avoid O(N^2) copying in VectoredIoUtil.mergeGcsObjectRanges
hypothesis: Accumulating merged underlying ranges lazily in a single ImmutableList.Builder per combined group inside VectoredIoUtil.mergeGcsObjectRanges (instead of calling GcsObjectCombinedRange.union on every step, which copies all prior ranges into a new ImmutableList and AutoValue instance each iteration) and using a static Comparator with ImmutableList.sortedCopyOf reduces range coalescing from O(N^2) time and allocation to O(N), proven by VectoredRangeCoalescingBenchmark.
learning: Replaced O(N^2) GcsObjectCombinedRange.union() copying and double-stream sorting in VectoredIoUtil.mergeGcsObjectRanges with primitive currentOffset/currentEnd tracking, lazy ImmutableList.Builder per coalesced group, and ImmutableList.sortedCopyOf(OFFSET_COMPARATOR, ranges). Improved all 9 VectoredRangeCoalescingBenchmark cases: up to -99.0% latency (2.71ms -> 27.2us, 100x faster) and -99.8% allocation (39.7MB -> 92.2KiB, 430x less memory) at ranges=4096, plus -21% to -44% on unmerged gapBytes=1048576 cases.
